name: HDFC Bank Ltd
about: HDFC Bank Limited (also known as HDFC) is an Indian banking and financial services company headquartered in Mumbai. It is India's largest private sector bank by assets and the world's tenth-largest bank by market capitalization as of May 2024. As of April 2024, HDFC Bank has a market capitalization of $145 billion, making it the third-largest company on the Indian stock exchanges. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 22.1% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 20.0%.
Revenue growth accelerated from 2% to 9% YoY over the last 4 quarters.

context.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
context.text: Thank you, Srini, and thank you, everyone. Let me start with the economic environment. The GDP growth in Q2 FY27 has been better than anticipated and high performance indicators such as industrial production, strong e-way bill, cargo activity, credit growth reflects sustained momentum. Retail consumption growth has also been robust with passenger vehicles, 2-wheeler sales all growing upwards of 30-plus percentage. Even consumer durables grew at about 11% year-on-year. This augurs very well for the economy, especially with the festive season underway. The broader policy environment has been supportive of economic activity. Alongside this, measures in the form of credit guarantee support to MSMEs have also been effective. RBI's proactive response through measures like the special FCNR (B) swap window generated record inflows, about $133 billion and helped stabilize the currency. With that background, let's take a quick look at how the business has been shaping up. We continue to strengthen our liabilities franchise, and it has been delivering with great vigor. Deposits increased 18.8% year-on-year on a reported basis, including a 4 percentage point lift from special FCNR (B) window. As you will see in our published deck, CASA grew at about 10.8% on an overall basis. And within this, retail CASA growth was about 11.2% year-on-year compared to 9% a year ago, reflecting improving momentum. We added about 1.7 million liability relationships in the second quarter, which is 25% higher than Q1 and 33% higher than the fourth quarter of last year. context.text: Yes. So, on the agriculture piece, I think we're all aware that we've had a shortfall in the monsoon, which has been also not very uniform given the peninsula as well as Northern India. Having said that, the actual sowing, for the kharif season has more or less remained constant with a marginal decrease of about 1.5% or 2%. And consequently, if we look through that, one would believe that the crop therefore should have the output, give or take a variance of about 3% to 5%. As of now, as of September, compared to June, our gross NPA on agri has remained largely constant. We've not seen any signs of concern or deterioration. It has held steady. And we will observe the situation as it unfolds. But as I said, what is encouraging is that the sowing has largely been about, you know, about 108 or 109 million hectares, which is just a marginally lower level than previous year.

context.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
context.text: I can take that. One is, coming on the interest expense side, you'll see that our cost of funds is flat quarter-to-quarter, at about 4.4% last quarter to this quarter. Sequentially, it has remained flat. Ideally, we would have expected that to be better. Better means lower. It didn't because of the mix of the FCNR deposits that came in. So, if you look at the deposit growth that we have had, 1.57 trillion, almost 1.3 trillion is the growth in time deposit. So, that outweighs from an overall cost mix point of view, and offsets the kind of a repricing on any of the back book that was coming in. So, that is why the cost of funds is flat. And also, one other aspect that in the cost of funds that you see is also some relief from the AT1 bonds that were called in August on the callable date. So, that was a relief, but then that relief was also through other, because we did have a borrowing for leverage, so, we did have borrowing offset that. So, that is why you see at an aggregate level, the cost of funds remained flat. That means the numerator by the denominator, you're looking at perhaps only the numerator of interest expense, but when you look at both, it's 4.4, which is on one of those pages which is published there. The second aspect of it that you asked about is the mix of the corporate bank. Yes, sequentially, the corporate bank has grown 2.8% in this quarter. Year-on-year, it is about 16.4%, which you're seeing in one of those Pages, Page 10 or something that you're seeing. If you're asking about how that mix will evolve over a period of time, I think both Sashi had mentioned it, but, Kaizad, you want to take that to say?

Nitin, we're just commencing the drive. Whilst demand is there, we just don't want to commit any number. Let it start to flow and you will see it. But definitely if the system is X, we will be a significant portion of the system as we were in the 2014, ‘15 period. That is our endeavour and I think we are all, you know, the entire team is quite gung-ho to mobilize that kind of we're all energized and I think we are on track towards that.

business.what_it_does: Large deposit-funded bank. Deposits grew 18.8% YoY in Q2 FY27 (4 percentage points of that from a special FCNR(B) window), and it added 1.7 million liability relationships in the quarter. Its lending includes an unsecured book, business banking, corporate and agri loans; the corporate bank grew 16.4% YoY. About 70% of the loan book is floating-rate. TTM revenue is INR359,956 crore and TTM PAT INR83,685 crore.

segments.name: Agri

credibility.label: medium
credibility.summary: Too early to score. The inputs hold four guidance items (NIM direction, December repricing, unsecured-book provision coverage, business-banking growth) and none can be tested against reported numbers. Management also declined to size the Q1 FY27 mobilisation drive (C4), so its guidance here is directional rather than numeric.

promises.evidence: The October 2026 25 bps rate change is due to be largely reflected in margins by December, given about 70% of the book is floating. Q3 FY27 has not been reported.
The inputs report no provision-coverage ratio for the unsecured book. No horizon was given.
The inputs report no business-banking growth. The only segment growth disclosed is the corporate bank at 16.4% YoY (C3), a different segment.
The inputs give no NIM series. Cost of funds was flat at 4.4% QoQ because FCNR time deposits offset back-book repricing (C3). Reported margin was 30.1% in Q2 against 30.6% a year earlier.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The liabilities franchise is 'delivering with great vigor': deposits up 18.8% YoY (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: 4 percentage points of that came from the special FCNR(B) window, so underlying growth was about 14.8%. CASA grew only 10.8%. Of the 1.57 trillion of deposit growth, about 1.3 trillion (83%) was time deposits, which kept cost of funds flat at 4.4% instead of falling (C3).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Margins can be neutral to positive from here as floating-rate repricing offsets the FCNR cost headwind (G1, G2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 revenue growth picked up to 9.4% YoY after 2.4%, 0.5% and 3.7% in the prior three quarters, but PAT grew only 5.8% and reported margin was 30.1% against 30.6% a year earlier. The December repricing has not been reported yet.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: No sign of agri stress despite the monsoon shortfall; kharif sowing was down only about 1.5-2% (C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Agri gross NPA was flat from June to September per management, but the inputs carry no agri NPA number and the crop outcome comes after the harvest.

bull.point: Deposit mobilisation: deposits +18.8% YoY (about 14.8% without FCNR), retail CASA growth up to 11.2% from 9% a year ago, and 1.7 million new liability relationships in Q2.
Revenue reaccelerated to 9.4% YoY in Q2 after three quarters of 0.5-3.7%. The corporate bank grew 16.4% YoY, and the AT1 call in August removed a cost line.
Asset-quality signals are steady: agri gross NPA flat in September against June despite the monsoon shortfall. Management expects the October rate change to reprice about 70% of the book by December.

bear.point: Earnings growth has slowed: Q2 PAT was up only 5.8% YoY against a 3-year PAT CAGR of 19.7%. Reported margin is down 670 bps over three years, and ROE is 14.0%.

Deposit growth is being bought with time deposits: about 1.3 trillion of the 1.57 trillion increase was term deposits, including FCNR, so cost of funds stayed at 4.4% and CASA growth of 10.8% trails total deposits at 18.8%.
Reliance on wholesale funding: borrowings are INR594,144 crore (0.98x equity), and new borrowing to support leverage offset the AT1 call relief.

questions: Of the 1.3 trillion of time-deposit growth, how much is special-window FCNR(B), at what all-in cost after the swap, and when does it mature? What is the NIM effect when it reprices or runs off?
With about 70% of the book floating and the October rate change flowing through by December, what Q3 FY27 NIM do you expect against Q2, net of the FCNR mix?

What were business-banking growth (against the 18-21% guide) and unsecured-book provision coverage (against mid-70s) in Q2 FY27? In which states is agri exposure most concentrated, given the uneven monsoon?
